text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal coagulation profile rules out hemophilia and von Willebrand disease, and the absence of fever or rash makes septic arthritis or acute rheumatic fever unlikely. Given the isolated knee swelling, family history, and negative bleeding workup, this presentation is most consistent with transient synovitis or early juvenile idiopathic arthritis, but the family history strongly suggests a genetic connective tissue disorder or hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia with atypical presentation; however, the most likely diagnosis given the context of "swelling" without bleeding diathesis in a toddler with family history is Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis
